## A Brazil tour featuring an excursion to Tijuca Forest

[Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) lies in Rio de Janeiro, where tropical forest blankets mountain slopes next to the built-up city. A single visit can reveal forest vegetation, waterfalls and views over the city. Our [half-day Tijuca Forest excursion](/brazil/tijuca-national-park/tijuca-forest-half-day-lunch/) is included in the current **[“Brazil for Groups: Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu and São Paulo” tour](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-sao-paulo-group-9-days/)**.

The journey lasts 9 days and crosses several parts of Brazil. Time in Rio is shared between the city's most famous attractions and the nature of the Atlantic Forest. Tijuca has a separate day within the sightseeing itinerary, so you do not need to combine the forest with an ascent of Corcovado or Sugarloaf Mountain in one short outing.

## Which day is devoted to Tijuca?

**Day four** of the group tour is devoted to Tijuca Forest. After exploring Rio, travelers enjoy a guided half-day walk. The excursion includes **an English-speaking guide and lunch**. The remainder of the day is free for resting after the walk or exploring the city independently.

The preceding days are different. Sugarloaf Mountain and a Rio sightseeing tour are planned for day two, and Corcovado and Santa Teresa for day three. Day five is devoted to flying from Rio to Foz do Iguaçu. This schedule reveals two sides of Rio: the lively oceanfront city and its forested mountains.

| Day | Main activity |
|---|---|
| 2 | [Sugarloaf Mountain and Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) |
| 3 | Corcovado and Santa Teresa |
| 4 | [Guided Tijuca Forest visit](/brazil/tijuca-national-park/tijuca-forest-half-day-lunch/) |
| 5 | Flight to Iguazu |

This is the exact day sequence of the nine-day itinerary. Other tours through Rio may use different excursions; a mention of the park on a route does not confirm inclusion of this specific half-day walk with lunch.

## What you will see in the forest

Tijuca forms part of Brazil's Atlantic tropical forest. The park is known for its combination of dense vegetation, mountain slopes, waterfalls and viewpoints. During a guided walk, visitors can experience how drastically the environment changes just a few kilometers from city neighborhoods: humid forest, streams and the tree canopy provide a different setting from Rio's waterfronts.

The standalone excursion is described as “tropical forest – waterfalls – viewpoints.” The exact sequence of stops, time spent on trails and specific viewpoints depend on how the selected outing is organized. **You should not expect to explore the entire national park in half a day**: the area is extensive, and the excursion covers selected accessible sections.

The main appeal of this itinerary is the combination of nature with a broader introduction to Brazil. The journey continues to Iguazu Falls and São Paulo, so Tijuca is one stage of a longer trip rather than the sole focus of the holiday.

## How the half-day excursion differs from other Rio outings

The [Brazil tour catalog](/brazil/tour/) includes itineraries visiting Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, historic neighborhoods and natural areas around the city. Each provides a different experience.

The [Tijuca Forest excursion](/brazil/tijuca-national-park/tijuca-forest-half-day-lunch/) emphasizes walks among trees and waterfalls, with stops at natural viewpoints. Corcovado visits usually center on Christ the Redeemer and panoramas of Rio. Sugarloaf Mountain reveals Guanabara Bay, the beaches and the city from a different angle. The nine-day group tour schedules these activities on separate days.

This is convenient for travelers: the afternoon is free after Tijuca, and the next day begins the journey to another region. A longer trek, a specialist birdwatching route or a full-day exploration of the park would need separate arrangements. None is specified as part of this half-day excursion.

## Preparing for half a day in tropical forest

Wear closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles and light clothing, and bring water and rain protection. Shady forest paths can remain damp even in warm city weather. Individual trails change after rain, and your guide adjusts the walk to actual conditions.

The excursion includes English-speaking guiding and lunch. A Russian-speaking guide must not automatically be assumed to be provided on this program; agree on language separately if needed. The same applies to a private format, special physical requirements and individual stopping points.

## Frequently asked questions about the Tijuca Forest tour

### How long is the forest walk?

The [standalone excursion](/brazil/tijuca-national-park/tijuca-forest-half-day-lunch/) lasts half a day. The remaining part of day four is free on the nine-day tour.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Lunch and the services of an English-speaking guide are specified in the excursion.

### Do I need to choose the excursion separately when booking the tour?

The [nine-day group itinerary](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-sao-paulo-group-9-days/) lists it as a separate excursion module on day four. Final inclusions are determined by the terms of your selected departure.

### Will I also see Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado on this tour?

Yes. Those sights are included on preceding days in Rio; after Tijuca, the itinerary continues to Iguazu and São Paulo.

lead: >-
  Fourteen days from Rio to Lençóis Maranhenses: wildlife watching in the Pantanal, the clear rivers of Bonito, the Amazon from Manaus and the white dunes of Maranhão. Learn how these distant regions connect, why the lagoon season matters and which domestic flights are excluded from the price.
---

## Amazing Brazil: 14 days from the Pantanal to the Amazon and Lençóis

This tour introduces the natural landscapes of several regions separated by vast distances. It begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), continues through the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) and [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/), heads to [Manaus and the Amazon](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/) and finishes in the state of Maranhão at [Lençóis Maranhenses](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/).

**Duration: 14 days and 13 nights.** The program suits travelers who want to experience different ecosystems in one journey, are comfortable with multiple transfers and domestic flights, and do not expect to spend half their vacation in one hotel.

## The route by region

| Days | Region and activity |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Urban panoramas of Rio |
| 3–5 | Pantanal, wildlife observation |
| 6–7 | Bonito, rivers and caves |
| 8–9 | Manaus, Amazon |
| 10–14 | São Luís, dunes and lagoons |

This is the main sequence, but it should not be understood as one continuous road trip. Flights are required between major regions, including connections via Campo Grande and Manaus. Domestic airline tickets **are not included** in the listed services and must be priced separately.

The benefit is variety: soon after sightseeing in Rio, the landscape, climate, transportation and methods of exploring nature all change. At the same time, this journey has far more logistical dependencies than a trip focusing on one natural region.

## Pantanal: wildlife watching rather than chasing one species

After a flight to Campo Grande, the itinerary enters the Pantanal. Open spaces, water, birds and reptiles are central here. The program includes a lodge stay, a horseback ride and time for wildlife observation. Weather affects the availability of particular activities; riding arrangements may change or be supplemented with another activity.

The Pantanal is best enjoyed by observing animals **in their natural habitat**, so no particular animal can be promised at a fixed hour. Treat each outing as a chance to see different birds and mammals rather than a guaranteed photographic hunt for one species.

The itinerary includes walks near waterways and possible additional fishing depending on conditions. The guide and current conditions determine how water-based activities are conducted safely; risky encounters with wild animals are not a guaranteed part of the trip.

## Bonito: crystal-clear water, waterfalls and caves

After the Pantanal, the journey continues to Bonito and the Serra da Bodoquena area. Nature here is different, with clear rivers, limestone caves, forest trails and waterfalls.

The route includes [Boca da Onça Waterfall](/brazil/place/boca-da-onca-waterfall/), the [Blue Lake Cave](/brazil/place/blue-lake-cave-bonito/) and the [Rio da Prata](/brazil/place/rio-da-prata/). A day visiting a cave and floating along a clear river differs from ordinary beach swimming: natural attractions generally have specified entry points, limited visit times and rules about equipment and conduct.

Nature activities in Bonito are subject to controlled visitor access, and weather can alter the availability of particular routes. Arrange the listed sights in advance while preserving some flexibility to change their order. This is especially important on a packed fourteen-day trip in which the next region requires a flight.

## Manaus: experiencing the Amazon by water and in the jungle

The next stage begins after a flight to Manaus. The program includes an evening canoe outing, a boat excursion, visits to local communities and a walk into the jungle with explanations of plants and animals.

Here it is important to distinguish **nature observation** from promises to encounter any particular animal. Water levels, rainfall and animal behavior affect what visitors see from the boat and on foot. The Amazon cannot be judged by the same standards as a fixed viewpoint or a city museum.

Some days feature demonstrations of traditional skills and fishing methods. These enrich the regional experience without turning the entire tour into a specialist fishing expedition or a survival course.

## São Luís and Lençóis: lagoons, dunes and the Preguiças River

The northeastern part of the journey begins in [São Luís](/brazil/place/sao-luis/), followed by a transfer to [Barreirinhas](/brazil/place/barreirinhas/). From there, visitors travel by four-wheel-drive vehicles to the dunes and freshwater lagoons of [Lençóis Maranhenses National Park](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/).

**The lagoons depend on the rainy season.** According to Brazil's conservation agency ICMBio, favorable conditions for full lagoons usually follow the rains, often from May to September. The itinerary has no fixed departure date, so your choice of month strongly influences the likelihood of full lagoons and comfortable walks.

The next day is devoted to the [Preguiças River](/brazil/place/preguicas-river/) and its riverside communities. Transport changes from jeep to motorboat, and the scenery from open sand fields to river landscapes, fishing villages and ocean views. The final stage includes a visit towards [Atins](/brazil/place/atins/) before returning to São Luís.

## What's included and who guides the trip?

The price includes **accommodation, meals according to the itinerary, excursions and transfers**. But guiding arrangements vary: **a private excursion with a Russian-speaking guide is provided in Rio, while the rest of the itinerary features group excursions with an English-speaking guide**.

Transport is mixed as well. Some journeys are private, while transfers between São Luís, Barreirinhas and São Luís and within Manaus are group services. This matters for travelers expecting a Russian-speaking escort throughout the entire trip.

**Excluded** are international and domestic flights, meals outside the program and additional excursions. When comparing the total cost with shorter itineraries, add the necessary air travel rather than focusing solely on the base tour price.

## When to choose this particular trip

If seeing larger animals and watching birds is your primary goal, spending more days in one natural region may be preferable. If you are drawn to unusual water landscapes, give more time to Bonito or Lençóis. “Amazing Brazil” is best for travelers who consciously choose **broad geographical exploration** over in-depth time in one place.

Compare [Brazil wildlife and nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/) with [adventure itineraries](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/). The former emphasizes wildlife watching and natural areas; the latter focuses on actual physical activities. A trip may combine both interests, but exertion varies by the individual days.

## Frequently asked questions about Amazing Brazil

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Domestic flights are explicitly listed among services paid separately. Their schedules must be agreed before the ground itinerary is finally confirmed.

### Is a Russian-speaking guide provided throughout?

No. Rio includes a private tour with a Russian-speaking guide; the other regions feature group activities led by English-speaking guides.

### Can I be guaranteed to see particular Pantanal animals?

No. Wildlife observation depends on season, weather and animal activity. The itinerary includes organized nature experiences but no guaranteed sightings of a particular species.

### When should I go to see the Lençóis lagoons?

Full lagoons are most likely following the rainy season. Check the seasonality of the northeastern leg before choosing dates; water levels between the dunes differ from month to month.

### Is this a relaxed or active tour?

The journey mixes viewpoints, nature walks, boat excursions and frequent transfers. You should be prepared to be active, but the level of exertion can be assessed day by day before booking.

## Amazon Clipper cruise on the Amazon: 3 days and 2 nights from Manaus

A short Amazon cruise offers the chance to see humid tropical rainforest from the water and discover nature far from the city waterfront. [Manaus and the Amazon](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/) are the starting point for river journeys through channels, lakes and flooded forest.

The [3-day Amazon Clipper cruise](/brazil/tour/amazon-clipper-cruise-traditional-3-days-2-nights/) includes **2 nights aboard**. The boat accommodates **up to 16 guests in 8 cabins**. Each cabin has air conditioning and a private bathroom; onboard facilities include a dining room, bar, library and open upper deck overlooking the river.

Prices start at **$1411**. The standard fare includes accommodation, full board, specified beverages, scheduled excursions, canoe outings with life jackets and the services of a naturalist guide speaking Portuguese and English.

## Day one: boarding in Manaus and a nighttime wildlife outing

Boarding takes place in Manaus. After meeting the vessel and crew, the riverboat sets off, leaving the urban waterfront for more densely vegetated riverbanks.

During the journey, the guide explains Amazonian ecosystems, seasonal flooding and the characteristics of the riverside forest. From the upper deck, travelers can watch the scenery change; channels and flooded banks look different as water levels vary over the year.

After dinner, there is an evening outing along the banks. Using flashlights, the guide searches for caimans and other nocturnal animals. Frogs, snakes, night birds and sloths may be seen in the wild, but these are free-ranging animals, and sightings of any particular species cannot be guaranteed on every outing.

## Day two: Janauacá Lake, rainforest and fishing

Early in the morning, guests take a canoe outing on [Janauacá Lake](/brazil/place/janauaca-lake/). It is a good time for watching birds and river wildlife, including pink river dolphins found in this region. Travelers then return for breakfast and set out on a guided forest walk.

On the walking section, the guide discusses tropical plants and how Amazonian residents use forest resources. The itinerary includes an introduction to a local community; lake-area residents cultivate cassava and fruit, fish and gather forest products.

**Piranha fishing** is scheduled for the afternoon. It is one hands-on activity within a nature cruise, not a standalone multi-day fishing expedition. Another canoe outing follows dinner for the sounds and sights of the nocturnal forest.

## Day three: Janauari Park and the Meeting of the Waters

The third day's itinerary visits [Janauari Ecological Park](/brazil/place/janauari-ecological-park/). Here travelers explore flooded forest areas by canoe and along wooden boardwalks. Giant Amazon water lilies, with their large round leaves, grow in these waters. The ability to see particular plants and animals depends on the season and water level.

The vessel then heads towards the Meeting of the Waters near Manaus, where the dark Rio Negro flows alongside the lighter Solimões River. Differences in temperature, density and current speed keep their waters visibly distinct at the surface for some distance. It is one of the best-known natural sights near Manaus.

Afterwards, the boat returns to the city waterfront, passing the port and other riverside districts, and the cruise ends.

## What's included and what costs extra?

| Included | Extra expenses |
|---|---|
| Cabin, 2 nights | Transfers before and after the cruise |
| Full board | Personal expenses and tips |
| Excursions and canoe outings | Insurance |
| Water, tea and coffee | Other drinks outside the package |

Guiding is provided by a naturalist speaking **English and Portuguese**. No Russian-speaking guide is specified for this cruise. Alcoholic beverages and other soft drinks beyond the included allowance are charged separately.

The route and the order of water excursions may change with the season, water levels, weather and other natural conditions. If you plan to fly out of Manaus after the cruise, allow enough time between the ship's return and your flight.

## Who will enjoy the three-day format?

Three days work for travelers who want to include the Amazon in a longer Brazil itinerary or discover the river ecosystem for the first time. On a small vessel like this, the principal experiences are canoe outings, forest sounds and wildlife observation, rather than a long list of onboard entertainment options.

For longer river journeys, compare [Brazil cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/brazil/), [wildlife and nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/) and other [Brazil itineraries](/brazil/tour/). Key differences are the number of nights afloat, distance from the city and excursions actually included.

## Frequently asked questions about Amazon Clipper

### How many guests can the riverboat accommodate?

Amazon Clipper accommodates **16 guests in 8 cabins**. Each cabin has its own bathroom and air conditioning.

### Are meals included?

Yes. Full board means breakfasts, lunches and dinners as specified in the itinerary. Drinking water, tea and coffee are included as well.

### Can I see pink dolphins?

They occur around Janauacá Lake, but a sighting on any given morning cannot be guaranteed. The cruise follows living ecosystems and seasonal conditions.

### Are transfers to the boat included?

No. Transfers to the boarding point and after the cruise are paid separately. Confirm the exact departure place and time with the organizer.

## Survival in the Amazon rainforest: four days of hands-on experience

This tour focuses on activities rarely included in a standard Amazon sightseeing trip. **4 days and 3 nights** are spent in tropical forest and a base camp. Instead of a series of city attractions, the program features canoeing, traditional fishing techniques, searching for natural resources, building a shelter and sleeping in hammocks.

The journey appeals to travelers who want practical experience in the forest under an instructor's supervision. It is worth considering everyday conditions beforehand: some nights are spent away from a conventional hotel, and activities involve a humid climate, water and long periods outdoors.

## What participants do each day

| Day | Main activity |
|---|---|
| 1 | Camp, canoeing, fishing techniques |
| 2 | Finding water, food, fire, shelter |
| 3 | Independent practice under instructor supervision |
| 4 | Return and the Acajatuba area |

**Day 1: getting to know the camp.** The group leaves the hotel for the base camp. The first day covers canoe handling and local fishing techniques using nets, spears, arrows and cast nets. Guests spend the night in hammocks at the base. It is a gradual transition from conventional sightseeing to forest life.

**Day 2: practical skills.** The instructor demonstrates how to find water, light fires, identify edible plants and construct a shelter. First aid and tree climbing using a traditional method are also mentioned. After lunch, participants practice these skills. The evening brings dinner in the forest, an introduction to local customs and a night in hammocks fitted with mosquito nets between the trees.

**Day 3: doing things yourself under supervision.** Participants forage for ingredients and prepare food using techniques learned the previous day. The activities remain part of an organized program with an instructor. Another night is spent in the forest.

**Day 4: returning and a river excursion.** After returning to the base camp, the group visits the area around [Acajatuba village](/brazil/place/acajatuba-village/) (Vila do Acajatuba), with a dolphin encounter planned. The group then returns to the pier.

## How this differs from an ordinary Amazon excursion

Standard nature itineraries devote much of their time to boat journeys, guided walks and wildlife watching. On the survival program, the central activity is **what participants actually do for themselves**. You need to follow your instructor carefully and be ready for unfamiliar sleeping conditions.

Sleeping in a hammock differs from staying in a lodge. Mosquito nets are provided for the forest nights, but there is no hotel comfort in the forest. Before booking, discuss health considerations, tolerance of heat and humidity, any experience sleeping outdoors and personal equipment requirements.

To consider other activities, compare [Brazil adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/) and [wildlife and nature itineraries](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/). Not every Amazon boat tour involves survival training.

## Inclusions and price

The paid services include **river transfers, a guide, the camp and the listed activities**. Hotel accommodation is not included. Meals specifically mentioned in the day-by-day program form part of the forest experience; it would be inaccurate to extend that to any restaurant or hotel services.

Participation costs **$4225 per person**, with a minimum group size of **4 people**. Compare this with an organized four-day adventure, not the cost of a single river outing or one night in a conventional lodge.

Preparation and safety deserve particular attention. Safety on the water, in plant selection and during forest activities depends on the briefing and on following group rules. The program introduces practical techniques but does not mean that four days qualify someone to survive independently without a guide.

## Who is this journey for?

The route appeals to active travelers who want a holiday filled with hands-on activities and are ready for two nights in the forest. It is less suitable for people who need constant access to hotel facilities and prefer a relaxed, mainly sightseeing-based schedule.

For a journey that also includes major cities and waterfalls, consider the [Rio – Amazon – Iguazu itinerary](/brazil/tour/rio-de-janeiro-amazon-iguazu-falls/). It has a different focus: several regions in one trip, without a multi-day survival program.

## Frequently asked questions about the survival tour

### How long is the program?

Four days and three nights. The first days focus on camp and learning skills, while the final day involves the return and a visit to the Acajatuba area.

### Do participants sleep in standard hotels?

Forest overnight stays are in hammocks, including those with mosquito nets. A separate hotel is explicitly excluded from the price.

### Do I need previous independent trekking experience?

No specific minimum trekking experience is stated, but physical demands and sleeping arrangements should be assessed before joining. Training takes place with an instructor.

### What's included in the price?

River transport, a guide, the camp and scheduled activities. The minimum group is 4 participants.

### Can I see dolphins?

The fourth day includes a trip to the Acajatuba area for a dolphin encounter. Wild animal behavior depends on natural conditions, so a particular sighting cannot be guaranteed.

lead: "This itinerary suits travelers who want to experience the Amazon by water and air over 3 days, stay at Mirante do Gavião and devote a day to the Anavilhanas Archipelago area. The key questions are how the seaplane flight works, how the program changes between low and high water, what is included and which excursions remain optional."
---

## Who is the three-day Amazon VIP tour for?

Three days in the Amazon allow you to combine an unusual transfer, accommodation at a riverside lodge and substantial nature excursions without changing hotels repeatedly. The journey starts in Manaus, continues along the Rio Negro and around the [Anavilhanas Archipelago](/brazil/place/anavilhanas-archipelago/), then returns to Manaus. Its defining features are **a comfortable base and private excursions on a short journey**.

On day one, after meeting a guide, the program includes an approximately 30-minute seaplane flight above the Rio Negro. Landing is associated with the stay at Mirante do Gavião Amazon Lodge. Day two focuses on the river, villages and forest; day three on the Meeting of the Waters of the Rio Negro and Solimões, pink dolphins and the return to the airport.

For an Amazon visit with a different lodge and a visit to Acajatuba village, compare this journey with the [four-day “Amazon” itinerary](/brazil/tour/amazon/). If you prefer moving along the river continuously and sleeping in a cabin, consider the [Tukano cruise](/brazil/tour/amazon-tucano-cruise/).

## Day one and the seaplane transfer

[Manaus](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/) is the gateway to land and river routes through the Brazilian Amazon. On arrival, an English-speaking guide meets the travelers, followed by a road transfer to the pier. The flight then begins over the dark Rio Negro and its forested islands.

The seaplane serves as both transport and a sightseeing experience: passengers see the river from above before checking in. Main luggage is transported separately by road, with an estimated delivery time of 3 hours. It is sensible to keep documents, medications, sun protection and immediate essentials in your hand luggage. Check permitted hand-luggage weight and contents for the specific flight.

Your base is Mirante do Gavião Amazon Lodge on the Rio Negro. The lodge has 13 suites, a pool, spa facilities, a pier and the CamuCamu restaurant. Dinner is included on the first evening; additional drinks are paid separately. It is well suited to visitors who want to return to the same lodge after forest and river excursions.

## Anavilhanas during low water and high water

[Anavilhanas National Park](/brazil/place/anavilhanas-archipelago/) changes as Rio Negro water levels rise and fall. During low water, sandy beaches emerge and some activities are on foot. At high water, forest areas become accessible by boat and the route may pass through flooded forest known as *igapó*. According to ICMBio, low water in the park generally occurs around September–February, while high water is roughly March–August; actual timings shift each year.

**The low-water version of day two** includes a speedboat trip to the Santo Antonio and Tiririca communities, a forest walk, lunch with local residents, Tiririca beach and a visit to a large Macucu tree.

**The high-water version** passes through the Sobrado community, rainforest trails, a visit to a samaúma tree, lunch in a local house and the Paraná das Araras area. The natural focus remains, but the actual stops differ. Choose travel dates based on the experience you prefer: sandy river beaches or flooded forest.

Possible wildlife includes sloths, birds, caimans and tapirs, helping illustrate the ecosystem, but sightings of wild species cannot be guaranteed in advance. For other nature-focused itineraries, explore [Brazil wildlife and nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/).

## What happens on the final day?

On the journey back towards Manaus, the route passes the famous Meeting of the Waters, where the dark Rio Negro and light-brown Solimões flow side by side with a visible boundary for some distance. Differences in the waters' composition, temperature, density and currents help explain the contrasting colors and slow mixing.

A program involving Amazonian pink dolphins follows. The permitted forms of interaction with the animals are determined by the rules at the specific location and instructions from the guides. Respect restrictions designed for the safety of both people and dolphins, and do not expect animal behavior to be guaranteed. After the river excursion, lunch and a transfer to Manaus airport are scheduled.

For more regional geography, read about [Manaus and the Amazon](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/) or browse the [Brazil tour catalog](/brazil/tour/) for other programs.

## Included services and optional activities

The tour price covers accommodation at Mirante do Gavião according to the program, the day-one seaplane flight, private excursions and transfers, entrance tickets and an English-speaking guide. Meals follow the schedule: dinner on day one; breakfast, lunch and dinner on day two; breakfast and lunch on day three.

Two additional activities are worth considering: diving in the Rio Negro and a nighttime boat excursion to observe animals. Both are **charged separately** and must not be assumed to be part of the standard package. Drinks and personal expenses are also excluded. Russian-language guiding requires separate agreement; the standard guide is English-speaking.

The main tour page specifies prices, accommodation options and booking terms. Before booking, check arrival and departure flights, the seaplane's luggage rules, the relevant seasonal river itinerary and availability of optional outings.

## What to prepare for the journey

The main practical feature is the combination of air, road and river transport. Pack light quick-drying clothes, closed-toe shoes for possible forest walks, insect repellent and rain protection. A waterproof case is useful for a camera or phone. Plan separately for the first hours before your main luggage arrives by road.

The trip lasts 3 days and 2 nights, so a delayed inbound flight could shorten day one. Coordinate arrival with seaplane departure and leave a sensible margin before your return flight. If required, we will confirm the sequence of transfers and excursions for your selected dates.

## Frequently asked questions about the Anavilhanas VIP tour

### Can I experience Anavilhanas in 3 days?

Yes. The second day is dedicated to the archipelago's river and forest routes, while days one and three involve arrival and the journey back through Manaus. The exact content of day two depends on water levels.

### Is the seaplane flight included in the price?

Yes. The day-one seaplane flight is included. Main luggage is delivered separately by vehicle; confirm baggage allowances and delivery timing for your departure.

### Do I need special skills for jungle walks?

The program includes walking and boat outings, but no mandatory advanced sporting fitness is specified. Check the accessibility and difficulty of specific trails and any health-related restrictions before traveling, especially in the rainy season.

### Is a nighttime wildlife outing included?

No. The night boat excursion is an optional service. Confirm whether it can be arranged on your dates and its separate price.

### How does this tour differ from an Amazon cruise?

Here, you spend 2 nights at a fixed lodge and arrive by seaplane. On the [Tukano cruise](/brazil/tour/amazon-tucano-cruise/), the cabin is aboard the vessel and river travel forms the core of the entire itinerary.
